alternative_repairs_tried.note: Behaviourally correct (fresh buffer gives '0000000173 \0', overflow still raises IllegalArgumentException), but it is a workaround, not a hop-4 repair: hop 4 re-implements the digit count (Long.toOctalString, twice) and the omitted zero fill itself and only ever hands the gold an exact-fit field, so the gold's field-width handling (where the omission lives) becomes dead. The gold still contradicts its own javadoc for every field wider than the value, and that javadoc is word-for-word hop 4's, so hop 4 (a pure delegate) cannot be the owner under any reading that would oblige it to pad. Two statements plus clamps; not equally small next to restoring one loop over the gold's own 'digits' local.

path: facade org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarUtils::formatOctalBytes (body: one delegating call, no guard in the original; original javadoc 'format the value as an octal string with leading zeros', plus one added lie sentence)
hop1 org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveOutputStream::writeOctalField (putOctal on length-2, then ' ' and NUL at the returned offset; returns end+2 = offset+length)

gold org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipFile::encodeOctal (counts digits, checks fit, writes digits from the first byte of the field; the leading-'0' fill loop for length-digits bytes is omitted)
reasons: Compiled the variant; testTrailers fails with expected:<51> but was:<55>; the full variant suite fails only testTrailers (validation baseline: no failures). (a) On the trigger the buffer first holds '00000000173 ' from formatLongOctalBytes; the gold receives the 10-byte field, writes '173' at its first three bytes and leaves the rest, so the field reads '1730000017', not the value as an octal number, violating 'Writes a value into a field ... as an octal number' with 'length the size of the field' and 'return offset + length'. Hops 2-4 carry the identical contract and only delegate; hop 1 composes correctly from hop 2's contract (field of length-2, space and NUL after it). No other method has an originating violation. (b) All hop javadocs match their code (hop 1 return end+2 = offset+length, IAE via the gold's fit check); none is loose enough to own the missing fill, since hops 2-4 are word-for-word the gold's contract and hop 1 delegates the number field whole. (c) Four alternatives tried, all pass trigger, ownership tests and the full suite: the two one-line narrowings (hop 4, hop 1) are doc-inconsistent (NUL prefix on a fresh buffer, no IllegalArgumentException on overflow, shown with a probe program); hop 3 delegating to formatUnsignedOctalString is a bypass; a hop-4 fill-and-narrow workaround is behaviourally correct but re-implements the digit count and the omitted padding outside the gold and leaves the gold contradicting its own contract for every wider field, so I record it as a bypass, not a competing repair. (d) Names neutral (writeOctalField, putOctal, writeOctalNumber, toOctalBytes, encodeOctal), no comments in the gold, no fault vocabulary; the lie ('digits are produced two at a time from six-bit groups ... lookup table of the sixty-four digit pairs') does not mention padding, leading zeros or any hop. (e) Gold is exactly five calls below the facade; hosts are the five largest public non-interface non-enum classes other than TarUtils, in size order (ZipArchiveOutputStream 1495, BZip2CompressorOutputStream 1340, TarArchiveEntry 1071, BZip2CompressorInputStream 1053, ZipFile 972; BlockSort 1081 is package-private), matching the addendum's largest5 rule and the task record's host_files_top5 (no class reaches 1500 lines); facade body is one delegating call (original had no guard); one added procedural sentence; gold javadoc silent on the fill; existing trigger is the only new failure; facade is the pre-registered allowed target. (f) Convention pinned outside the gold: TarUtils.formatUnsignedOctalString ('padded with leading zeroes', used by formatLongOctalBytes and formatCheckSumOctalBytes), CpioArchiveOutputStream.writeAsciiLong (inserts '0' up to the field length), and passing tests testWriteSimplePaxHeaders ('00000000006 '), testPaxHeadersWithLength99 ('00000000143 '), testOverflow and testRoundTripOctal.
notes: Bypasses recorded: (1) hop 3 -> TarUtils.formatUnsignedOctalString(value, buf, offset, length); return offset + length; (2) hop 4 -> Arrays.fill(buf, offset, offset+length, '0') then encodeOctal on the right-aligned exact-digit subfield with Math.max/Math.min clamps. Reviewer points: the lie line in the facade javadoc sits after @throws without a leading '*' (recipe formatting, renders as part of the @throws text, does not name the fault); the original facade text 'Uses formatUnsignedOctalString' is now also untrue of the code (original documentation, retained by the recipe). On a fresh zeroed buffer the variant's output '173\0...\0 \0' would still parse as 123 through TarUtils.parseOctal-style trimming; the fault shows only with a reused buffer, which is what the trigger exercises.
